headline: Ratchet & Clank source gets readable names, shared types and more data built from C
summary: Ratchet & Clank's decompiled source was reorganised around shared types, readable names and folders grouped by system. The changes retain the reported 5116 of 5116 matched functions: matching means the compiled functions have exactly the same bytes as the original game. Data work raised the reported share of compiled data to 74%, with values generated from the user's own game image.
highlights: Shared headers replace repeated declarations and private views of player, camera and object data (#171, #172, #174, #175, #177).
Button, level and player state names replace numeric values throughout the source (#188, #189, #190).
Data blocks and pointer references now build from C without committing retail values (#196, #197, #198).
Checks and tools identify suspect matching tricks, remove unnecessary ones and guard against regressions (#194, #195, #204).
